subtopic: Throughput vs latency trade-off / Batch-size lever
learningObjective: Reason about the throughput vs latency trade-off in LLM serving and identify how batch size affects each metric.
stem: Select all correct statements about the throughput vs latency trade-off in LLM decode serving. (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: Increasing batch size always reduces both TPOT and total request latency because more compute is used in parallel per step; there is no downside to arbitrarily large batches other than memory limits.

Increasing batch size amortizes weight-HBM reads across more requests, raising aggregate tokens/second (throughput), but each batched step takes slightly longer (because of extra compute and possibly attention I/O), so per-request TPOT increases mildly.
Latency and throughput are the same metric expressed in different units (1/latency = throughput); optimizing one always optimizes the other.

Beyond some batch size, the workload transitions from memory-bandwidth bound to compute-bound; further batch-size increases raise per-step compute time proportionally with fewer amortization gains, giving diminishing returns on aggregate throughput and larger per-request TPOT penalties.

explanation: B is correct: batching amortizes weight reads (good for throughput) but each batched step is slightly slower per-request (bad for TPOT). D is correct: as batch grows, the operator transitions from bandwidth-bound to compute-bound and further gains diminish while TPOT rises. A is wrong: larger batches raise TPOT (per-token latency per request), so latency and throughput trade off. C is wrong: throughput = tokens/sec across all users; latency = time per request. They are not reciprocals and can move independently.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: throughput up, per-request TPOT up.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: bandwidth→compute transition and diminishing returns.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: throughput and latency are different metrics.

assumptions: 'Latency' = per-request TPOT or total request latency.
'Throughput' = aggregate output tokens/sec across all users.
nonImplications: Does not imply the optimal batch size is universal; it depends on SLA constraints.
Does not imply that continuous batching removes this trade-off; it only makes the batch composition dynamic.

performanceClaim.scope: Batch-size lever for throughput vs latency in LLM decode
